title: Updating the app is only ever tested from the one release just before
what: Before a release, the cloud installs only the newest published version and updates it to the new one. Members who skipped a few updates (for example still on a version from a month ago) jump several steps at once, and that jump, with all the data changes in between, is never tried. The conditions test also starts only from the last release.
expected: The update is also tried from the oldest version still in use (or a few versions back), with real data, before a release.
fix_line: Add a second update check that starts from an older release still in use

title: Only the GitHub copy of the phone app is proven to update; the watch app and the Play copy never are
what: The release run proves that the phone app downloaded from GitHub updates in place and keeps its data. The watch app and the copy installed from Google Play are never updated from an older version in any cloud test, so a watch update that loses its saved settings or a running rest, or a Play update problem, is only found by members.
expected: The watch app and the Play copy each get the same keep-your-data update check before they go out.
fix_line: Run the same update check for the watch app, and one for the Play build

title: The cross-role test never lets time pass: no plan running out, staff removed or gym paused
what: The test that drives the member app, the admin app and the server together covers orders, cancels, messages, a desk check-in, a file import and the gym colour. It never checks what each side sees when a member plan ends, a member leaves and comes back, a staff member is removed, or a gym is paused or closed.
expected: The cross-role test also covers a plan ending, a staff member losing access, and a paused gym, checked on both apps.
fix_line: Add plan-end, staff-removed and gym-paused journeys to the cross-role test

title: The new-feature dots test makes a fresh install look like an old one, so it never checks that a brand-new member sees no dots
what: The owner asked on 15 Nov that a first install shows no new-feature dots. The cloud phone test of the dots starts from a fresh install and then wipes what the phone counts as already seen, which puts the dots back. So no screen test checks the brand-new-member case; only a small rule test does.
expected: One phone test opens a real fresh install without wiping what was seen and checks that no dot shows.
fix_line: Add a fresh-install step to the dots test that expects no dots
